title: fix: compare integer64 logical tweaks by value
description:
## Summary

Restore this PR to a reviewable state on current `main` while keeping the original `data_logical` fix narrow.

## Thanks to maintainers

Thanks for maintaining `DBItest`, and for the earlier discussion in `#308` and `#309` about keeping `logical_return` narrowly scoped.

## Issue or motivation

`data_logical` still failed for a `logical_return` tweak that returns `bit64::integer64` values, including the list-returning form discussed in `#309`. After this branch was refreshed against current `main`, the restored CI workflows also could not resolve the existing `constructive` Suggests dependency from the default CRAN/RSPM repository set.

## Root cause

The original spec compared fetched values with `expect_identical()`, so a backend returning `1L`/`0L` did not match `bit64::integer64` logical-return expectations despite representing the same logical values. Separately, the generated stream-bind specs needed explicit `stringsAsFactors = FALSE` for character bind-value data frames. The later CI failures were dependency metadata failures: `constructive` is used by the package, but the GitHub Actions dependency solve runs under a repository override that does not include the package source.

## Change

- Convert `data_logical` expectations into scalar predicates that compare by logical value.
- Cover both vector-returning and list-returning `logical_return` tweaks for `bit64::integer64` values.
- Keep generated stream-bind specs aligned with the helper by emitting explicit `stringsAsFactors = FALSE`.
- Keep the roxygen-generated Arrow write-table Rd wrapping from the formatter suggestion.
- Merge current `main` into this PR branch so the restored workflows and version bump from `#574`/`#575` are included.
- Add `https://cynkra.r-universe.dev` as an `Additional_repositories` entry, and pass `cynkra/constructive` to the CI dependency setup paths that otherwise ignore that repository during the initial solve.

## Tests

Latest refresh on current PR head `13b43f7c`:

- `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE='https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest' Rscript -e 'pak::lockfile_create(c("deps::.", "any::sessioninfo", "r-lib/lintr", "local::.", "cynkra/constructive"), dependencies = c("Config/Needs/lint", "all"))'` — pass.
- `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE='https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest' Rscript -e 'pak::lockfile_create(c("deps::.", "any::sessioninfo", "any::rcmdcheck", "r-lib/roxygen2", "any::decor", "r-lib/pkgdown", "r-lib/covr", "any::xml2", "any::rmarkdown", "cynkra/cynkratemplate", "deps::.", "cynkra/constructive"), dependencies = c("Config/Needs/build", "Config/Needs/check", "Config/Needs/website", "Config/Needs/roxygen2", "all"))'` — pass.
- `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE='https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest' Rscript -e 'pak::lockfile_create(c("deps::.", "any::sessioninfo", "any::pkgbuild", "any::remotes", "decor", ".", "cynkra/constructive"), dependencies = c("Config/Needs/check", "all"))'` — pass.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — pass.
- `Rscript -e 'lintr::lint_package()'` — pass, no lints found; local config warns that `expect_shape_linter` is not in current defaults.
- `Rscript -e 'testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-logical-return.R", reporter = "summary")'` — pass, 62 assertions.
- `Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(reporter = "summary")'` — pass, 9693 passed, 64 skipped, 0 failed.
- `R CMD build .` — pass, built `DBItest_1.8.3.9012.tar.gz` from a fresh temporary directory.
- `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_=false R CMD check --as-cran DBItest_1.8.3.9012.tar.gz` — pass with 2 NOTEs: development version number and local HTML Tidy not recent enough for HTML validation.

## Scope

This stays within the `data_logical` roundtrip spec, generated bind-spec alignment, CI dependency resolution for an existing Suggests package, and branch sync needed to keep this PR reviewable. It does not change broader integer64 comparison behavior, backend workflow design, backend-specific test semantics, or other bigint-related specs such as `#311` or `#412`.

title: feat: Specify the schema of Arrow results
description:
The Arrow specs so far never look at a schema: `check_arrow()` converts every stream or array with nanoarrow's default ptype and compares data frames, so an `int64` column silently becomes a double (9007199254740993 comes back as 9007199254740992), and nothing says whether a backend exposes the schema before the first batch, whether it stays the same across chunks or across `dbBind()` executions, or what a zero-row result carries. This PR adds six specs that pin this down.

## New specs

- `arrow_fetch_arrow_schema` (`R/spec-arrow-fetch-arrow.R`): `nanoarrow::infer_nanoarrow_schema()` on the object returned by `dbFetchArrow()` gives a struct schema with one child per column, named like the columns, before any batch is consumed, and the stream can still be consumed to the expected data frame afterwards.
- `arrow_get_query_arrow_schema` (`R/spec-arrow-get-query-arrow.R`): the same for `dbGetQueryArrow()`.
- `arrow_get_query_arrow_schema_zero_rows` (`R/spec-arrow-get-query-arrow.R`): a zero-row result (the existing `WHERE (1 = 0)` query) still has a complete schema, with as many children as columns and the column names. The child formats are deliberately not pinned: they differ between backends for such a query (RSQLite's native path gives `null`, DBI's default path gives `bool`).
- `arrow_fetch_arrow_chunk_schema` (`R/spec-arrow-fetch-arrow-chunk.R`): every array returned by `dbFetchArrowChunk()` carries the schema; names and formats of the children are identical across all chunks of a 25-row result, including the zero-length chunk fetched once `dbHasCompleted()` is `TRUE`. The loop runs until completion since the chunk size is implementation-specific, and the concatenated chunks are compared with the expected data frame.
- `arrow_read_table_arrow_64_bit` (`R/spec-arrow-read-table-arrow.R`): a column written with `dbWriteTable(field.types = c(a = "BIGINT"))` comes back from `dbReadTableArrow()` as an `int64` column (format `l`), and `nanoarrow::convert_array_stream(stream, to = data.frame(a = bit64::integer64()))` yields the exact values as `integer64`. Guarded with `skip_if_not_installed("bit64")`; `bit64` is added to `Suggests`.
- `arrow_send_query_schema_stable` (`R/spec-arrow-send-query-arrow.R`): for a table created from `data.frame(a = c(1L, 2L))`, a `SELECT a FROM <table> WHERE a = <placeholder>` sent with `dbSendQueryArrow()` and bound twice with different values via `dbBind()` returns chunks whose children have identical names and formats, for every placeholder pattern of the context.

The specs are gated with `skip_if_not_dbitest()` at `1.8.3.1` to `1.8.3.6`. This continues the repo's `<release>.<counter>` convention: the `1.7.99.N` gates were added before 1.8.0, the `1.8.0.N` gates while `DESCRIPTION` was at 1.8.0.9005, and the last release is 1.8.3. Backends opt in by declaring `dbitest_version >= "1.8.3.6"`; a context that declares `"1.8.1"` (as the RSQLite test context does) skips all six with the usual `tweak: dbitest_version` message.

## Documentation

- The paragraph about `nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream()` in `spec_arrow_get_query_arrow` had landed in the "Failure modes" section for lack of a section tag. It now opens a "Specification" section, matching `spec_arrow_fetch_arrow`, and the new paragraphs join it there.
- `man/*.Rd` is regenerated with `devtools::document()`.
- With `bit64` in `Suggests`, roxygen2 finds the topics `factor` and `ordered` in both base and bit64 and warns about the unqualified links in `spec_driver_data_type` and `spec_meta_bind`. The second commit qualifies them as `[factor][base::factor]` and `[ordered][base::ordered]`, which renders identically, and regenerates the inlined bind specs that embed that prose as comments (four one-line changes).

## What stays as it is

The three `arrow_write_table_arrow_roundtrip_64_bit_*` specs (and their `arrow_append_table_arrow_*` twins) remain skipped with "Internal: Need to enhance test_arrow_roundtrip()". Un-skipping them is not just a matter of passing a `to` argument to `check_arrow()`: `dbWriteTableArrow()` has no `field.types`, and DBI's default `dbCreateTableArrow()` maps an `int64` stream through `nanoarrow::infer_nanoarrow_ptype()` to a double column, so with DBI's defaults the value is written as `REAL` and the "character" variant (full decimal representation) cannot hold. Making them meaningful needs an Arrow-side way to declare the column type, which is a separate decision; the new `arrow_read_table_arrow_64_bit` spec covers the read side through `dbWriteTable()`, which every backend supports.

## Verification

`DBItest::test_arrow()` with the RSQLite context from `tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R` (declaring `dbitest_version = "1.8.3.6"`, `NOT_CRAN=true`), DBI 1.3.0, nanoarrow 0.9.0:

- CRAN RSQLite 3.53.3, which relies on DBI's default Arrow methods (run in a `callr::r()` subprocess with a separate library first on the path): 153 tests, 137 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped; the 16 skips are the pre-existing `!date_typed`/`!time_typed`/`!timestamp_typed` tweaks and the six "Internal" skips above. All six new specs pass.
- A development build of RSQLite (3.53.3.9012) with native Arrow methods: 153 tests, 125 passed, 12 failed, 16 skipped. All six new specs pass. The 12 failures (`arrow_read_table_arrow`, `arrow_read_table_arrow_empty`, and the `_integer`/`_logical`/`_character`/`_blob`/`_mixed` roundtrip specs of `dbWriteTableArrow()` and `dbAppendTableArrow()`) are the same 12 on `main` with that build: its native path returns SQLite integers as `int64`, which `expect_identical()` against R integer columns rejects. They are unrelated to this change.
- With `dbitest_version = "1.8.1"` both builds skip exactly the six new specs. `tests/testthat/test-consistency.R` passes, `tools::checkRd()` is clean for every touched topic, and `devtools::document()` reports no new warnings.

## Issues

Related to #412: the new 64-bit spec pins `int64` in the schema and a lossless `integer64` conversion for values beyond the 32-bit range, but not the edge cases between 2^55 and 2^63 or the treatment of `-2^63` and `NULL` that the issue asks for.

Related to #334: a strict `bigint` mode affects `arrow_read_table_arrow`, and the new `arrow_read_table_arrow_64_bit` spec sits in the same family.

Related to #292: the unconditional skips of the Arrow 64-bit roundtrip specs stay in place, for the reason given above.

No open issue is closed by this PR.

- the generated-file comment at the top;
- a blank line after `<!-- badges: start -->`, and a doubled blank line collapsed to one;
- ` ```r ` written as ` ``` r ` (four code blocks);
- `---` written as a full-width row of hyphens;

title: ci: Document with a patched roxygen2 that keeps the sentence gap
description:
Split out of #563 so it can be decided on its own.

## The problem

commonmark discards the whitespace a line break stands for. roxygen2 turns every softbreak into a bare newline, so the `.Rd` carries a line break with nothing after it and `Rd2txt()` renders it as a single space. Prose written one sentence per line therefore comes out single-spaced, while the same words wrapped to a fixed width with two spaces after the period keep the gap.

That makes the two styles mutually exclusive: splitting a sentence pair separated by two spaces silently drops one of them. That is what forced the very long single roxygen lines this package used to carry, because joining was the only way to keep the gap.

Only the text renderer is affected. `Rd2HTML()` and `Rd2latex()` differ by whitespace that HTML and TeX collapse — and LaTeX applies its own sentence spacing regardless. But text is what `?topic` shows, so it is the version most people read.

## The change

A new composite action, `.github/workflows/roxygen2-fork`, installs roxygen2 from upstream with the `R/` part of `krlmlr/roxygen2@f-sentence-spacing` applied on top, and `R-CMD-check.yaml` runs it immediately before the Roxygenize step.

It shallow-clones upstream, fetches the branch, computes the diff against their merge base restricted to `R/`, and applies it with `git apply --3way`. Restricting to `R/` means an unrelated upstream change to a test fixture cannot fail the documentation step. It aborts if the patch is empty or does not apply, rather than silently installing an unpatched build, and afterwards asserts that what it installed really carries the patch.

`Config/roxygen2/version` becomes `8.1.0.9100`. The `.9100` suffix distinguishes a patched build from upstream's own `.9000` development builds; if upstream moves, the `x.y.z` part follows it and the suffix stays. `DESCRIPTION` is DCF and cannot carry a comment line — `read.dcf()` rejects one as malformed — so the explanation lives in a `Config/cynkra/roxygen2` field.

## Why it is a separate pull request

Taking it changes rendered help across the package; leaving it means the reformatting below renders exactly as the package renders today, with one space between sentences. Neither half needs the other to be correct, so they should be able to be decided separately.

`man/` is not edited by hand here. The `.Rd` files are generated output, so CI roxygenises and commits them itself — they arrive on this branch as an automated commit rather than in the hand-written diff. That commit has already landed: 58 regenerated `.Rd` files are part of this pull request's diff, and the hand-written half stays reviewable on its own.

## Upstream

The roxygen2 side is `krlmlr/roxygen2#8`, on the fork, not yet filed with r-lib. It is deliberately narrow: mid-sentence breaks are untouched, links are unaffected, and two guards keep it from firing wrongly — an abbreviation list so a line ending in `e.g.` or `et al.` does not gain a mid-sentence gap, and a fix for a determinism bug where a line starting with `\doi{}` or `\code{}` gained or lost its gap at random, because the test was reading roxygen2's own random placeholder for protected Rd tags.

title: ci: Point the `backends` and `odbc` workflows at the central install action
description:
## What was broken

Every run of the `backends` and `backends odbc` workflows failed in under a second. The `RSQLite` and `RKazam` jobs (from `backends.yaml`) and the `mysql` job (from `odbc.yaml`) all died at the step `Run ./.github/workflows/install` with:

```
Can't find 'action.yml', 'action.yaml' or 'Dockerfile' under '/home/runner/work/DBItest/DBItest/.github/workflows/install'. Did you forget to run actions/checkout before running your local action?
```

Everything after that step was skipped. Because these workflows also run on `pull_request`, every open PR in the repository showed red `backends` checks and `mergeable_state: unstable`, masking real failures.

## Why

The composite actions moved out of each repository's `.github/workflows/<name>/` and into `cynkra/cynkratemplate/.github/actions/<name>/` in 94c5747a. That commit rewrote all eighty references across fifty-eight files, but `backends.yaml` and `odbc.yaml` were not among them. They kept pointing at `./.github/workflows/install`, which no longer exists here — a recursive listing of `.github/workflows/` shows only workflow `.yaml` files plus the `revdep2/`, `revdep4/` and `revdepx/` script directories.

The central action is a drop-in. It accepts all four inputs these call sites pass — `token`, `needs`, `extra-packages`, `cache-version` — with unchanged meanings; diffing it against the copy 94c5747a deleted shows the two files are identical apart from the action's own two nested references (`get-extra` and `get-website`, which became central for the same reason).

## Also in these two files

Both changes only start to matter now that the install step runs at all.

**`RSPM` removed.** It was pinned to `https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/focal/latest` — a retired hostname, and Ubuntu 20.04 binaries for a job that runs on `ubuntu-24.04`. This is not inert: `r-lib/actions/setup-r` reads `RSPM` from the environment first and only derives the right URL from the runner's codename when that variable is unset (`setup-r/src/installer.ts`, `let rspm = process.env["RSPM"] ? ... : "NULL"`, and the codename lookup is guarded by `rspm === "NULL"`). So the stale value would have won over the `use-public-rspm: true` that the install action passes to `setup-r`. Dropping it matches every already-migrated workflow here, none of which sets `RSPM`; `R-CMD-check` is green on `main` with exactly that configuration.

**`actions/checkout` bumped from `v3` to `v6`**, which the other twenty-seven call sites in this repository already use. The two remaining `v4` call sites are in `claude.yaml` and `lint.yaml` and are out of scope here.

## Deliberately left alone

The `custom/before-install` and `custom/after-install` references in `R-CMD-check.yaml`, `R-CMD-check-dev.yaml` and `pkgdown.yaml` look similarly broken but are not. They are each repository's own hooks rather than central ones, and all twelve call sites are guarded by `if: hashFiles('.github/workflows/custom/<name>/action.yml') != ''`, so they skip cleanly in a repository like this one that has no `custom/` directory. Serving them centrally would give every repository the same hooks, which is the opposite of what they are for.

## Validation

GitHub Actions cannot be run locally, so: both files parse as YAML; no `uses: ./` reference remains in either; and every `uses:` resolves to a ref that exists (`cynkra/cynkratemplate@main` carries `.github/actions/install/action.yml`, and `actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/upload-artifact@main`, `ankane/setup-mariadb@v1` and `ankane/setup-postgres@v1` all resolve).

Opening this PR exercises both workflows for real, since each runs on `pull_request`. The bar for this change is that the jobs get past the install step. Any failure after it is a genuine backend problem and pre-existing — none of the three jobs had reached that far since 94c5747a, so this PR is the first run that could show one. All three are green.

## Also in this PR: the minimum R version

A second, unrelated change, requested by the maintainer: `DESCRIPTION`'s `Depends:` floor moves from `R (>= 3.2.0)` to `R (>= 4.1)`. That floor was many releases behind what the package assumes in practice, so raising it stands on its own merits.

The stated motivation was to silence the `lint` job, and the bump alone does not do that. `lint.yaml` runs `lintr::lint_package()` with `LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT: true`, against the repository's `.lintr.R`, which starts from `all_linters()` and subtracts a curated list of exclusions. The job reported four warnings, all of one kind:

```
R/spec-meta-bind-arrow-stream.R:423:9: warning: [strings_as_factors_linter] Supply an explicit value for stringsAsFactors for this code to work before and after R version 4.0.
R/spec-meta-bind-arrow-stream.R:455:32: warning: [strings_as_factors_linter] Supply an explicit value for stringsAsFactors for this code to work before and after R version 4.0.
R/spec-meta-bind-stream.R:563:9: warning: [strings_as_factors_linter] Supply an explicit value for stringsAsFactors for this code to work before and after R version 4.0.
R/spec-meta-bind-stream.R:595:32: warning: [strings_as_factors_linter] Supply an explicit value for stringsAsFactors for this code to work before and after R version 4.0.
```

Those same four were annotated on the `lint` run for `main` at 31bb2807 and on this PR's head before the third commit below, with the identical `Process completed with exit code 31` — so the run before the bump and the run after it were the same.

`strings_as_factors_linter()` takes no arguments and never reads the declared R dependency. It flags any `data.frame()` or `read.table()` call that passes unnamed character arguments without an explicit `stringsAsFactors=`, on the grounds that the default flipped in R 4.0, and it does so regardless of what `DESCRIPTION` says. The linter that *does* take an R version, `backport_linter()`, is active here and reports nothing. It defaults to the running R rather than to `DESCRIPTION`, and in any case has nothing to flag: the package contains no native pipe `|>` and no lambda shorthand `\(x)`.

For the record on where the red came from: `lint` was green on `main` through 97e9a397 and first failed at 31bb2807 (#563), which added both flagged files.

Two version checks become dead code once the floor is 4.1. Both are noted rather than changed, since both still evaluate correctly and neither blocks the build:

- `tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R:38` — `if (getRversion() < "4.0") "stream_bind_too_many"`, now always false
- `vignettes/DBItest.Rmd:13` — `knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = (getRversion() < "3.5"))`, now always `FALSE`

There is no `backports` dependency to drop.

## Also in this PR: retiring `strings_as_factors_linter`

A third change fixes those four `lint` failures, by dropping the linter rather than by changing the code it flags.

**Why the flagged code cannot simply carry the argument.** `R/spec-meta-bind-stream.R` and `R/spec-meta-bind-arrow-stream.R` are generated. `tests/testthat/helper-dev.R` inlines the test bodies from `R/spec-meta-bind-expr.R` and `R/spec-meta-bind-runner.R` and deparses them with `constructive::construct()`. Editing the four call sites by hand would be undone the next time `load_all()` regenerates the files, so the argument would have to come from `constructive` — and there is no setting for it. Its `data.frame` constructor only ever appends `row.names` and `check.names` to the call it builds; `stringsAsFactors` appears in that constructor solely as a name it guards column names against colliding with, never as an argument it emits. `constructive::opts_data.frame()` takes just `constructor` and `recycle`. Of the other constructors, `read.table` cannot round-trip these unnamed columns at all (it errors with `more columns than column names`), and `list` replaces every `data.frame(...)` in the generated files with `list(...) |> structure(class = "data.frame", row.names = ...)`, rewriting all of the generated output to dodge one warning. That leaves a `gsub()` over the generated text in `helper-dev.R`, which is more machinery than the check is worth.

**Why retiring the linter is safe.** It exists to catch code whose meaning changed when `data.frame()`'s `stringsAsFactors` default flipped to `FALSE` in R 4.0. With `Depends: R (>= 4.1)` the package can never run under the old default, so the linter has nothing left to protect.

**What changed.** Three lines inside the existing `modify_defaults()` call in `.lintr.R`, adding `strings_as_factors_linter = NULL` to the list of exclusions it already subtracts from `all_linters()`. Because the config file already exists and already works by subtraction, this cannot accidentally swap the active set for a different one.

Verified locally with the r-universe build of `r-lib/lintr` at 3.4.0.9000 — the same dev version `lint.yaml` installs via `extra-packages` — and with `DBItest` and `cyclocomp` installed, so that the local run sees the same linters and the same files as CI:

- The active linter set goes from 98 to 97. Diffing the sorted name lists before and after shows one removal, `strings_as_factors_linter`, and no additions.
- `lintr::lint_package()` before: `N = 4`, the same four `[strings_as_factors_linter]` warnings CI reported, and nothing else.
- `lintr::lint_package()` after: `N = 0`, `ℹ No lints found.`

title: docs: State the goals and non-goals
description:
A reader landing on this README should be able to tell in a few seconds whether DBItest is for them — and for this package the answer is "only if you are writing a backend", which is worth saying outright.

Every bullet is drawn from the repository:

- **"primarily useful for developers of DBI backends"** — the README's own wording.
- **"Not all tests can be satisfied"** — `vignettes/DBItest.Rmd` says exactly that, and gives the contradictory `logical` roundtrip tests as the example. That is the basis for the non-goal about not demanding every backend pass everything.

description:

The payoff is sentence-level diffs. A reworded sentence touches one line instead of reflowing the paragraph around it, so review sees the change and not the rewrap.

`README.md` is edited directly here — this package has no `README.Rmd`, so the markdown is the source rather than a build product.

`R/spec-meta-bind.R`, `-arrow`, `-stream` and `-arrow-stream` are generated from `R/spec-meta-bind-expr.R` by `tests/testthat/helper-dev.R`, and they embed the feeder's prose as comments together with its source line numbers. Regeneration would not have happened on its own: `helper-dev.R` skips it when `CI` is set, and otherwise triggers on a file modification time comparison that a fresh clone makes meaningless. Left alone, the drift would have surfaced as a large unrelated diff in whoever next regenerated locally.

`man/` is not part of this pull request. Every commit in the chain leaves the `.Rd` files byte-identical to `main`, and CI regenerates and commits them after merge, so what is under review here is the sources and the files generated from them.

- Every `R/*.R` still parses.
- The regeneration is idempotent: two consecutive runs produce the same four files.

A line break which follows the end of a sentence currently renders as one space, not two, so writing one sentence per line drops the sentence gap from the rendered help. title: ci: fix `backends odbc` workflow (unixODBC headers + MariaDB driver install)
description:
## Problem

The scheduled `backends odbc` workflow has been failing for over a month. The `matrix` setup job succeeds, but the `mysql` backend child job fails. Fixing it surfaced two independent causes, addressed in two commits.

## Cause 1 — missing unixODBC development headers

The job failed at **"Install locally to avoid error with test_local()"** (`R CMD INSTALL revdep-dev/odbc`) with:

```
<stdin>:1:10: fatal error: sql.h: No such file or directory
ERROR: configuration failed for package 'odbc'
```

Compiling `odbc` from source needs the unixODBC **driver-manager** development headers (`sql.h`) + `libodbc`, from `unixodbc-dev`. The database-specific driver steps only install *drivers*, not the driver *manager*; the `mysql` path (the only active matrix entry per `revdep-dev/Makefile`) never installed `unixodbc-dev`. The earlier "Install package and dependencies" step hit the same error but hid it, because `R_REMOTES_NO_ERRORS_FROM_WARNINGS: true` demotes it to a warning.

**Fix:** add an always-run (Linux) step installing `unixodbc-dev` before the source build.

## Cause 2 — MariaDB ODBC driver never installed

With the headers in place, the source build now succeeds and the job reaches **"Test backend"**, which then failed with:

```
[unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib '/usr/lib/libmaodbc.so' : file not found
```

`.github/odbc/install-mariadb-driver.sh` downloaded a pinned focal-only build (3.1.9) from `downloads.mariadb.com`, which returned **HTTP 522** (CDN origin timeout). With no `set -e`, the failed download was masked — "Setup MySQL" reported success but `libmaodbc.so` was never installed.

**Fix:** install the driver from the Ubuntu archive (`odbc-mariadb`) instead, matching how the other backends install their drivers. It also pulls in `libmariadb3` with the connector-C auth plugins (e.g. `caching_sha2_password` for MySQL 8) in their default location, so the manual plugin placement is dropped. `odbcinst.ini`'s `[MySQL Driver]` now points at the package path (`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/odbc/libmaodbc.so`), and `set -e` is added so a future install failure is no longer silently ignored.

## Verification

- `odbc.yaml` parses as valid YAML; new step ordered before the odbc source build.
- Confirmed on Ubuntu 24.04 that `unixodbc-dev` provides `/usr/include/sql.h` and that `odbc-mariadb` installs a loadable driver at `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/odbc/libmaodbc.so` (all shared-lib deps resolve); unixODBC reads the repo `odbcinst.ini` via `ODBCSYSINI` with `[MySQL Driver]` present.
- The first fix is already confirmed by CI: on the previous PR-head run the `R CMD INSTALL revdep-dev/odbc` step went from failing to passing.

> Note: the separate `lint` check is red due to pre-existing `pipe_consistency_linter`/`expect_shape_linter` findings in `R/spec-*.R` and `R/utils.R` (the `lint` workflow has failed on `main` since well before this branch). Those files are untouched by this PR, so that failure is unrelated.

title: ci: Fix MySQL ODBC backend workflow
description:
## Problem

The `backends odbc` workflow (`.github/workflows/odbc.yaml`) has been failing on its `mysql` job. Investigating the [failing run](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBItest/actions/runs/29954472543) showed three interacting failures:

1. **`system_requirements()` installs nothing.** The step runs `remotes::system_requirements("ubuntu", "24.04", …)`. The **CRAN release** of `remotes` (2.5.0) that CI installs does not yet know Ubuntu 24.04 — its supported list stops at 22.04 — so the call aborts with a `match.arg()` error that is hidden by the `done < <(…)` process substitution. No system dependencies are installed, including `unixodbc-dev`, and the `odbc` package then fails to compile:

   ```
   <stdin>:1:10: fatal error: sql.h: No such file or directory
   ------------------------- ANTICONF ERROR ---------------------------
   Configuration failed because odbc was not found.
   ```

   (The **dev** version of `remotes` does list 24.04, but it is unreleased and not on CRAN.)

2. **The MariaDB driver never installs.** `install-mariadb-driver.sh` downloads pinned `3.1.9` `ubuntu-focal` tarballs from `downloads.mariadb.com`, which now return **HTTP 522**. Because the script used `set -x` but not `set -e`, it silently continued, leaving no driver installed. The `focal` builds are also incompatible with the `ubuntu-24.04` runner (they need `libssl1.1`).

3. **`odbcinst.ini` pointed at the wrong path** (`/usr/lib/libmaodbc.so`), the location the old tarball wrote to.

## Fix

- Install the dev version of `remotes` (`github::r-lib/remotes`), which knows Ubuntu 24.04, so `system_requirements("ubuntu", "24.04", …)` succeeds and yields `unixodbc-dev`. The query stays aligned with the actual runner OS.
- Replace the tarball download with an apt install of `unixodbc-dev` and `odbc-mariadb`. `odbc-mariadb` pulls in `libmariadb3`, which ships the authentication plugins (including `caching_sha2_password`, required for MySQL 8) in its default plugin directory — so no manual plugin installation is needed.
- Add `set -e` to the driver script so install failures surface instead of being silently ignored.
- Point the `[MySQL Driver]` entry in `odbcinst.ini` at `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/odbc/libmaodbc.so`, where the `odbc-mariadb` package installs the driver.

## Verification

- `apt-get install unixodbc-dev odbc-mariadb` installs `libmaodbc.so` at the configured path; `ldd` resolves every dependency (against `libssl.so.3`/`libcrypto.so.3`, present on noble).

title: fix: replace legacy `PST8PDT` time zone with `America/Los_Angeles` in roundtrip tests
description:
## Problem

The timestamp roundtrip specs use `"PST8PDT"` as an arbitrary non-UTC time zone (alongside `"GMT"` and `"UTC"`) in `roundtrip_timestamp` and `roundtrip_timestamp_extended`, for both the SQL and Arrow write/append table specs.

`PST8PDT` is a POSIX-style **legacy** zone. Recent `tzdata` splits these legacy zones (`PST8PDT`, `EST5EDT`, `CST6CDT`, `MST7MDT`, `EST`, `MST`, `HST`) out of the main `tzdata` package into a separate `tzdata-legacy` package. I verified this in a fresh `ubuntu:26.04` container (`tzdata 2026b`):

- installing **main `tzdata` only** → `PST8PDT` and the other POSIX zones are **absent**;
- `tzdata` does **not** even `Recommends: tzdata-legacy`, so a default install never pulls it in;
- installing `tzdata-legacy` restores them.

On such systems `lubridate::with_tz(x, "PST8PDT")` emits `Unrecognized time zone 'PST8PDT'` and falls back to UTC — which fails the tests (and silently loses the distinct-offset coverage the column is meant to provide). (On Ubuntu 24.04 these zones were still in the main package, so the failure is new to 26.04.)

## Fix

Use **`America/Los_Angeles`** instead. It is the canonical modern IANA successor to `PST8PDT` — identical PST/PDT −8/−7 behavior including DST — and as a `Continent/City` zone it ships in **core** `tzdata`, present in essentially every environment (verified present in 26.04's main `tzdata`). The specific zone is arbitrary for the purpose of these tests; this one keeps the exact same semantics while being universally available.

Because a `Continent/City` name contains a `/`, it cannot double as the column name (the transform derives the target zone from `toupper(names(out))`). It is therefore mapped explicitly in the roundtrip transform, exactly the way `"LOCAL"` already is:

```r
tz <- toupper(names(out))
tz[tz == "LOCAL"] <- ""
tz[tz == "LOS_ANGELES"] <- "America/Los_Angeles"
```

## Files changed

Both timestamp roundtrip test cases in each of:

- `R/spec-sql-write-table.R`
- `R/spec-sql-append-table.R`
- `R/spec-arrow-write-table-arrow.R`
- `R/spec-arrow-append-table-arrow.R`

## Verification

Confirmed in R (4.5.3) that `America/Los_Angeles` is in `OlsonNames()`, that the roundtrip transform normalizes input and output identically, that instants are preserved, and that the old `"PST8PDT"` path warns `Unrecognized time zone` when the zone is unavailable.

title: fix roundtrip timestamp
description:
This fixes two small issues with timestamp comparisons.
 
First PST is not a time zone. R accepts it without error but effectively uses UTC instead. See this R session: I am currently in the Paris timezone. If I use PST8PDT which is a proper timezone,  it shows 9 hours behind as it should.

```
> test <- Sys.time()
> test
[1] "2016-12-29 10:24:31 CET"
> as.POSIXlt(test, "PST")
[1] "2016-12-29 09:24:31 PST"
> as.POSIXlt(,test, "PST8PDT")
[1] ""2016-12-29 01:24:31 PST"
```
Second when comparing timestamps, I think we need to use equivalent instead of equal, because two timestamps with the same epoch but different timestamps would be different objects.

title: Dates should be numeric internally, not integers
description:
This is consistent with base R dates, which are always constructed as numerics

``` r
str(unclass(as.Date("2016-01-01")))
#>  num 16801
str(unclass(Sys.Date()))
#>  num 17107
```

This is true of [base::as.Date.default](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/45b3b3d6256b7c4cf94834b00f187388d523b25b/src/library/base/R/dates.R#L73) and the other coercion methods in that file.  Also output as numeric in [readr](https://github.com/tidyverse/readr/blob/37d6eda5b2e52707bfa6ea2db8d52e0209796615/src/Collector.h#L101).

If there are cases in base R where Dates are constructed as integers it seems like they are the exception rather than the rule and are likely bugs.

@hadley mentioned he was previously confused on this issue.

Associated issues, https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/1303, https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/issues/86#issuecomment-151783522, https://github.com/rstats-db/DBItest/issues/9
